title: Measure, number and weight
src: Wisdom of Solomon, Wisdom 11:20, 24 · World English Bible
author: Wisdom of Solomon
lines: but you arranged all things by measure, number, and weight.
For you love all things that are,
and abhor none of the things which you made;
For you never would have formed anything if you hated it.
why: Two lines that belong together. The first says the world is ordered, so it can be measured and understood; medieval scholars quoted it to defend the study of nature. The second says why it was made at all: out of love. Say it when you look at anything well made, a leaf, a bridge, a piece of music, and remember that order and love are not rivals.

title: Into whatever houses I enter
src: Hippocrates, The Oath · tr. Francis Adams (1849)
author: Hippocrates (attributed)
lines: I will go into them for the benefit of the sick,
and will abstain from every voluntary act of mischief and corruption;
why: The heart of the oath that doctors swore for two thousand years: whoever lets you in, you are there for their good, not your own. It is worth carrying into any house, ward, office or classroom where people trust you with themselves.
